requirements.heading: RIP_TEXT
requirements.text: The current drawing position is set immediately to the right of the drawn text. Subsequent Line, Circle or other such commands will not affect this position. This provides a means so that you can quickly do another RIP_TEXT command (presumably in another color) at a later time and have the text show up immediately after the previous text (even after subsequent graphical operations like circles, rectangles, lines, etc).

requirements.heading: RIP_TEXT
requirements.text: **IMPORTANT NOTE:** Note that this "current graphics cursor location" is only updated for horizontal text moving from left-to-right in "left justified" mode. Any other orientation does not reset the location! _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: RIP_TEXT_XY
requirements.text: This command is an efficient combination of [RIP_MOVE](#rip_move) and [RIP_TEXT](#rip_text). The text is drawn at the specified location according to the same settings that apply to RIP_TEXT (see above).

requirements.heading: RIP_TEXT_XY
requirements.text: The current drawing position is set immediately to the right of the drawn text. Subsequent Line, Circle or other such commands will not affect this position. This provides a means so that you can quickly do another RIP_TEXT command (presumably in another color) at a later time and have the text show up immediately after the previous text. See the RIP_TEXT command for a more thorough discussion of this subject.

requirements.heading: RIP_TEXT_XY
requirements.text: This is the workhorse text command of the corpus (638 uses, versus zero bare `T` commands). In 3.x scenes it renders in whichever font was last selected - very often an [RIP_EXTENDED_FONT_STYLE](#rip_extended_font_style) outline font - and the text argument may contain `<<NAME>>` macros (`!|@809U<<LAB1>>` labels buttons from `.DEF`-file [text variables](../../glossary.md)) or `$&VAR$` dereferences. NEWS.RIP draws a drop-cap this way (`@A91G` + one large character) with the flowed article text starting mid-word after it (see the [drop-cap idiom](3.1-column-text-system.md#drop-caps)).

requirements.heading: RIP_BOUNDED_TEXT
requirements.text: Draws a text string that wraps and clips inside the given bounding rectangle. BOUNDS.RIP draws an `!|R2020A030` rectangle first ("Show our bounding box") and then issues this command with the _same coordinates_, making the layout unambiguous: four 2-digit corner coordinates, a 2-digit flags field (`00` observed), then the text (elided above). A one-shot boxed-text primitive, distinct from the [RIP_BEGIN_TEXT](#rip_begin_text)/[`1e`](3.1-column-text-system.md#defining-a-column-region---1e) flowed-column machinery.

The foreground text is drawn using the current foreground drawing color (set with [RIP_COLOR](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_color)). The shadow is drawn one pixel down and one pixel to the right of the font for both vertical and horizontal text. |
requirements.reason: Bitmap and classic stroke device kernels cover explicit scaling/matrices, vertical direction and shadows. Font-style/world/resolution policy, justification, cursor/style state, outline text and wire integration remain pending; BOLD scan painting is blocked by #17.

requirements.heading: Justification and Special Effect Flags
requirements.text: Flag values 1 and 2 are mutually exclusive. This means that either one of them may be specified, but not both! If both are omitted, then the text is "left justified". Flags 4, 8 and 16 are also mutually exclusive. If either of them are omitted, then the text is drawn with "top" justification. If both flags 1 and 2 are specified, or more than one of the flags 4, 8 and 16 are specified then the command is considered an error and is completely ignored. _(v2.A4)_
requirements.reason: Bitmap glyph raster/metrics now support explicit device origins, integral scaling, vertical direction and shadows. Vector/outline fonts, justification/baseline, cursor/style/world state and wire integration remain pending.

requirements.heading: Dropshadowing
requirements.text: Here is how a font would look if it had dropshadowing enabled. The solid squares (█) are the foreground text drawn with the color set by the RIP*COLOR command, and the shaded squares (░) are the pixels drawn with the background drawing color set by the RIP_BACK_COLOR command. requirements.heading: Dropshadowing

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_FONT_STYLE
requirements.text: The outline-font command: scalable "Adobe and TrueType style" fonts with bold/italic/strikeout/underline facings, arbitrary alignment, and - new in 3.x - full rotation. This command is an extended form of the [RIP_FONT_STYLE](#rip_font_style) command: outline fonts draw the outline of each glyph and fill in the interior, scale to arbitrary point sizes (unlike the pre-defined sizes of RIP_FONT_STYLE), and carry special facing attributes (Bold, Italic, Strikeout, Underline). The commands [RIP_TEXT](#rip_text), [RIP_TEXT_XY](#rip_text_xy), [RIP_REGION_TEXT](#rip_region_text) and [RIP_BUTTON](4.3-buttons.md) use whichever font command is most recent (RIP_FONT_STYLE or RIP_EXTENDED_FONT_STYLE) - whichever font style has been selected will be the one used for rendering the associated text-related commands.

requirements.heading: The Shipped 3.x Wire Layout
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (FONTS.RIP crib; 430 uses); HLP; 2.x assets (SHADOW.RIP)._

requirements.heading: The Shipped 3.x Wire Layout
requirements.text: SyncTERM knows the opcode only as a four-field descriptor with no implementation; the RIPtel corpus shows the real 3.x argument block is far richer - **26 fixed characters followed by the font name**. TeleGrafix's own field-layout crib survives as a comment in FONTS.RIP (line 114):

requirements.heading: The Shipped 3.x Wire Layout
requirements.text:
```text
!|!sfFFFFZZOOSSCCBBCCWWRRRRRR
```

requirements.heading: The Shipped 3.x Wire Layout
requirements.text: decoding as `s`(1) `f`(1), `FFFF` 4-digit flags, `ZZ` size, `OO` orientation, then `SS CC BB CC WW` (2 digits each), and `RRRRRR` reserved. FONTS.RIP's rotation demo varies the `SS` field (`00` → `E4`, `gC`, …) under per-line labels "0 x 0", "180 x 90", "270 x 180" and so on - covering all **16 combinations of string rotation × character rotation** advertised for the 3.x font system. The common corpus idiom `…1a1a…` in the paired 2-digit fields reads as an x/y scale pair _(hypothesis)_, and TELLISTS.MNU comments narrate style flags directly ("Marin, centered, bold w/ dropshadow"). The observed layout does **not** match the 2.00a4 draft's 13-character argument list - and the rework happened **before RIPterm Professional 2.0 shipped**, not in 3.x: the SHADOW.RIP demo script in the 2.0 install (February 1995) already drives `y` with the 26-character block, `1a1a` idiom included (`!|y00000X02020000001a1a000000marin` - see the [RIPterm 2.30 icons README](../../2.0/assets/icons/README.md#shadowrip)).

requirements.heading: Font Names - the `.RFF` FastFont Families
requirements.text: _Evidence: HLP; corpus; assets ([3.x fonts](../../3.0/assets/fonts/README.md))._

requirements.heading: Font Names - the `.RFF` FastFont Families
requirements.text: Font names bind to the **`.RFF` "RIPscrip FastFont"** outline fonts (relabeled Atech FastFonts) that ship with RIPtel: families BRUSH, COBB, DEFAULT, DIXON, EUREKA, MARIN, OAKLAND, SYMBOL, each in 10 style variants (base, ` TH` thin, ` CN` condensed, ` WD` wide, ` EX` expanded, ` HO` hollow, and hollow combinations ` HT`/` HC`/` HW`/` HE`). The demos use Marin, Dixon, Cobb, and Symbol. The font-name argument may itself be a text variable: `!|y…000000$&FONT_NAME$` (SHOWFONT.FN). The five 2.00a4 predefined names (COURIER, HELV, TIMESROM, OLDENGL, SANSSERF) never appear in the corpus - nor did they ship: RIPterm 2.0's font set was already COBB/DEFAULT/DIXON/MARIN/SYMBOL, as `.FF1` files (see the [RIPterm 2.30 font assets](../../2.0/assets/fonts/README.md)). The `.RFF` file format is documented in the [2.0 FastFont techspec](../../2.0/techspecs/3.2-fastfont-fonts.md); RIPtel's three added families and regenerated catalog are in [FastFont Additions](../techspecs/3.2-fastfont-additions.md). If a specified font is not recognized, the default font of RIP_FONT_STYLE is selected (with size 1).

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4 (draft layout - wire positions superseded by the shipped 26-character block above; the parameter concepts survive in the shipping font system)._

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: > **Editor's note:** The sections below preserve the 2.00a4 draft's definitions of direction, alignment, point size and style. The shipped 3.0 driver reworked the wire layout (see the crib above) but the HLP error strings confirm the same concepts - plus string/character rotation, character spacing and shadowing the draft lacked. Draft field positions must not be used to author 3.x scenes.

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: **Text Direction.** The draft specified font direction in tenths (1/10's) of degrees for future expandability, with valid values 0.0 and 90.0 degrees (horizontal, and vertical bottom-to-top): `000` horizontal, `0P0` (MegaNum) = 900 = 90.0° vertical. _(v2.A2)_ The `<direction>` parameter was to be enhanced in a future revision to support arbitrary rotation of the font - which the 3.x system delivers as the string-rotation × character-rotation pairs demonstrated in FONTS.RIP. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: **Alignment.** The draft's `<h_align>` parameter: 0 = align left (X/Y location at the far left of the text), 1 = right align, 2 = center horizontally around the location. The `<v_align>` parameter: 0 = top of the tallest character, 1 = bottom of the tallest character, 2 = vertically centered (taking descenders into consideration), 3 = baseline at the X/Y base point.

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: **Point Size and Resolution Independence.** The `<size>` parameter defines the point size of the font to be displayed on the screen. In order to maintain resolution independence with extended fonts and various resolutions, a point size is formally defined as one physical pixel on a 640x480 resolution device. For other resolutions, the point size is adjusted proportionally - for example, a 1280x1024 resolution is exactly twice as wide as a 640x480 screen, but the height is 2.1333 times that of its 480 counterpart, so some adjustment must be made to be pixel-accurate. The ideal method is applying separate horizontal and vertical scaling to the font system; not all font systems allow this, so a "closest approximation" might have to occur. For the standard RIPterm resolutions of 640x350, 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768 and 1280x1024, only 640x350 and 1280x1024 do not have perfectly square pixels and need height adjustment. When getting into resolution independence, it is not always possible to get 100.0% pixel perfect accuracy.

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: **Style.** The `<style>` parameter defines the style in which the font is to be rendered, as flags which may be combined (OR'ed) together:

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | Style | Description        |

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | 00    | Normal font sizing |

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | 01    | Bold font          |

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | 02    | Italic font        |

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | 04    | Strike-out font    |

requirements.heading: The 2.00a4 Draft Parameter Semantics
requirements.text: | 08    | Underlined font    |

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: _Define a rectangular text region_

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `T`                             |

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x1:XY y1:XY x2:XY y2:XY res:2` |

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_begin_text)) · HLP (`RIP_BeginText`) · corpus (12 uses in N2_TITLE.RIP, NEWS.RIP) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16581)

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: This command defines a rectangular portion of the graphics viewport that is to display text, usually a long stream of text. Following this command should be a number of [RIP_REGION_TEXT](#rip_region_text) commands with the text to be displayed. The [RIP_END_TEXT](#rip_end_text) terminates this stream of text, something like this:

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text:
```text
RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
     RIP_REGION_TEXT
     RIP_REGION_TEXT
     RIP_REGION_TEXT
     :
     RIP_REGION_TEXT
RIP_END_TEXT
```

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: There must be at least one RIP_REGION_TEXT command in between the header and the footer. There may be as many as needed.

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: These commands ignore the current font "direction"; all text is always displayed horizontally in the current font type, style and size. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: NOTE: The `res` parameter is two bytes wide and is RESERVED for future use and should be set to "00".

requirements.heading: RIP_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: **3.x extension:** The 3.0 driver overloads the trailing "reserved" digits: NEWS.RIP chains four regions with trailing values `01`, `11`, `21`, `31` - column/stream selectors feeding the same flowed-text engine as [`1e`](3.1-column-text-system.md#defining-a-column-region---1e), linking the four page columns into one article stream _(field interpretation from census analysis)_. See [the legacy form in 3.1 Column Text System](3.1-column-text-system.md#the-legacy-form---1t-with-columnstream-digits).

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: _Display a line of text in rectangular text region_

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `t`                         |

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `justify:1` and text-string |

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1t <justify> <text-string>` **Example:** `!|1t1Southern California was pounded`

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Draw Color, Write Mode, Font Style, Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_region_text)) · HLP (`RIP_RegionText`) · corpus (42 uses in N2_TITLE.RIP) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16623)

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: A number of these commands may come sandwiched between the [RIP_BEGIN_TEXT](#rip_begin_text) and [RIP_END_TEXT](#rip_end_text) commands. The `<text-string>` should already word-wrapped in such a way that it will fit inside the rectangular region based on the current font, font size, and drawing color.

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: There are four possible settings for the `<justify>` parameter: _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: | Justify | Description                         |

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: | 0       | Left justify this line              |

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: | 1       | Right/left "full" justify this line |

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: If a text line falls off the bottom of the region, it is discarded -- the rectangular Text Region does not scroll.

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: This command is intended to import some sort of text file document directly into a RIPscrip scene and format it nicely to fit inside a simple rectangular area. If the `<justify>` parameter is set to a value of "1" for a given RIP*REGION_TEXT line, then that line will be justified to both the left and right margins (the RIP_BEGIN_TEXT boundaries). This is so that the displayed text aligns on both sides with the invisible boundaries. This "justification" is done by splitting each RIP_REGION_TEXT line up into chunks of word-groups, broken up at their "white-space" locations. Each spacer is then padded by however many pixels are necessary to keep each spacer of approximately equal size. Only enough spare pixels are added to make sure that the right-edge of the text region aligns with the right border of the boundary. The result is a nicely formatted text block. *(v1.54)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_REGION_TEXT
requirements.text: The corpus uses justify `1` for body lines and `0` for each paragraph's final line - N2_TITLE.RIP's article, quoted in full in the [census](../../3.0/research/riptel-script-census.md), is a TeleGrafix pitch for RIPscrip's JPEG/sound/24-bit future.

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: _End a rectangular text region_

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `E`      |

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `<none>` |

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1E` **Example:** `!|1E`

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (N/A) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_end_text)) · HLP (`RIP_EndText`) · corpus (20 uses in 8 files) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16090)

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: This command indicates the end of a formatted text block. Only one of these "end" commands is necessary for each block.

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: In 3.x it terminates both the 1.54 [RIP_BEGIN_TEXT](#rip_begin_text)/[RIP_REGION_TEXT](#rip_region_text) form and the 3.x [`1e` column-region](3.1-column-text-system.md#defining-a-column-region---1e) form, whose raw-text content runs until this command.

requirements.heading: RIP_END_TEXT
requirements.text: **HLP names without a known level-0 opcode.** Two drawing/state names in the RIPSCRIP.HLP inventory match no letter attested by any spec, corpus scene, or implementation: `RIP_TextMetric` (text-metric mode appears in HLP's text-window error strings) and `RIP_FontAttrib` ("Can't change system font attributes"). Their wire opcodes - if they ever had any - remain unknown. _Evidence: HLP._

requirements.heading: 3.1 Column Text System
requirements.text: _Reconstructed edition - every claim carries an evidence tag; see [Contents](README.md) for the legend._

requirements.heading: 3.1 Column Text System
requirements.text: A **flowed-text column system**: rectangular column regions, chained so prose pours from one into the next, paginated into overflow buffers and paged through with buttons.

requirements.heading: 3.1 Column Text System
requirements.text: Nothing in the published 1.54 or 2.00 Alpha 4 specifications resembles it, and there is no v1.54 or v2.0 counterpart to this page - the entire mechanism is reconstructed here from the RIPtel demo corpus, in which TeleGrafix left a field-map comment that decodes the core command. The [White Paper](../text/RIPScrip-3.x-technical-whitepaper.txt) points at it - to display "high-quality documents like those you would normally find in magazines or newspapers … you'd need to familiarize yourself with the multi-column system for extensive layout control" - RIPtel's help lists "multiple-column text displays ('news articles')" among RIPscrip 3.x's features, and the demo's own FONTSTOR.TXT advertises that "a powerful column system is" provided.

requirements.heading: 3.1 Column Text System
requirements.text: _Evidence: WP; HLP; corpus (FONTSTOR.TXT)._

requirements.heading: Defining a Column Region - `1e`
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (FONTS.RIP crib comment; NEWSPAPR.RIP, DEMO-01.COL and 6 more files)._

requirements.heading: Defining a Column Region - `1e`
requirements.text: The level-1 command `e` - absent from every published specification - opens a rectangular text-column region.

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: _Open a flowed-text column region_ _(hypothesized name)_

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Command** | `e` |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:2 y0:2 x1:2 y1:2 column:1 stream:1 flags:4 unknown:2 reserved:8` _(from TeleGrafix's crib; see below)_ |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1e <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <column> <stream> <flags> <cc> <reserved>` **Example:** `!|1e3W7DGRMD0100010000000000`

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Draw Color, Font Style, Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) _(inferred)_ **Evidence:** corpus (21 uses in 8 files: NEWSPAPR.RIP, DEMO-01.COL, N2_HORO.RIP, DBACK.FN, DRAGON.RIP and others; field map in FONTS.RIP) - not in the 2.00a4 spec, not in SyncTERM. Name _(hypothesis)_; HLP corroborates the mechanism (`RIP_SelectArticle`, "Invalid text article number", "Invalid text column number").

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: FONTS.RIP carries TeleGrafix's own positional field map as a comment directly above its use:

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text:
```text
!|! xxyyxxyycaffffccrrrrrrrr
```

requirements.text: which decodes as:

requirements.text: | Field | Chars | Meaning |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `xx` `yy` | 2+2 | Upper-left corner (x0, y0), [MegaNum](../../glossary.md) [world coordinates](../../glossary.md) |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `xx` `yy` | 2+2 | Lower-right corner (x1, y1) |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `c` | 1 | Column number within the stream |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `a` | 1 | Article/stream number |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `ffff` | 4 | Flags - `0001` observed on every region fed by `1R` with pagination, `0000` on inline clipped regions _(bit 0 = enable overflow buffering, hypothesis)_ |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `cc` | 2 | Unknown - always `00` in the corpus |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: | `rrrrrrrr` | 8 | Reserved - always zero in the corpus |

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: A real region from the newspaper demo, decoded:

requirements.heading: RIP_EXTENDED_BEGIN_TEXT
requirements.text: `4L,3D`-`91,9K` = (165, 121)-(325, 344) in the standard 1280×960 world frame; column `0` of stream `1`; flags `0001`. Text drawn into the region uses the current font ([`y`](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_extended_font_style) / [`Y`](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_font_style)) and colors, and is word-wrapped to the region's width.

requirements.heading: Column Content - Raw Text Lines and `1E`
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWSPAPR.RIP, N2_HORO.RIP, NEWS.RIP)._

requirements.heading: Column Content - Raw Text Lines and `1E`
requirements.text: Once a column region is open, content follows as **raw text lines** - lines with _no_ `!|` introducer at all, a wire-format novelty with no 1.54/2.0 precedent. The block is terminated by `1E` ([RIP_END_TEXT](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_end_text), the 1.54 command in a new role). From NEWSPAPR.RIP's front-page "INSIDE" teaser boxes:

requirements.heading: Column Content - Raw Text Lines and `1E`
requirements.text:
```text
!|1e0F3M434G0100000000000000
Southern California was pounded
with nearly two weeks of rain.
Hundreds left homeless as a result.
!|1E
```

requirements.heading: Column Content - Raw Text Lines and `1E`
requirements.text: The parser is therefore modal: between `1e` (or its legacy equivalent, below) and `1E`, non-command lines are article prose, not garbage. Blank raw lines separate paragraphs (N2_HORO.RIP flows 30 raw lines through three columns this way).

requirements.heading: Column Content - Raw Text Lines and `1E`
requirements.text: Content can equally be flowed in by [RIP_READ_SCENE](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_read_scene) (`1R`) pointed at a plain `.TXT` file, an `$OVERFLOW(stream,…)$` page, or a `$&VARIABLE$` - see [Flowing Whole Files](#flowing-whole-files---1r-on-plain-text) below.

requirements.heading: Chained Columns and Streams
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (DEMO-01.COL, N2_HORO.RIP, NEWSPAPR.RIP, DBACK.FN)._

requirements.heading: Chained Columns and Streams
requirements.text: Multi-column layout comes from opening _several_ regions with ascending column numbers that share one stream number, then flowing content once. Text fills column 0, continues into column 1, then 2, and so on. The horoscope page chains three:

requirements.heading: Chained Columns and Streams
requirements.text: Streams are independent articles: the newspaper front page runs its main story as columns 0-2 of stream 1 and its secondary story as a region marked column `3`, stream `2` (`1eA17FH48Y3200010000000000`) - column numbers evidently need not restart at zero for each stream. Each stream paginates and resets separately (see Overflow, below).

requirements.heading: The Legacy Form - `1T` With Column/Stream Digits
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWS.RIP, N2_TITLE.RIP)._

requirements.heading: The Legacy Form - `1T` With Column/Stream Digits
requirements.text: The 1.54 command `1T` ([RIP_BEGIN_TEXT](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_begin_text)) defined a text region with a two-digit reserved tail. RIPscrip 3.x quietly reinterprets that tail as the same `c`,`a` pair, so 1.54-syntax files can feed the column system. NEWS.RIP builds a four-column newspaper page entirely this way:

requirements.heading: The Legacy Form - `1T` With Column/Stream Digits
requirements.text:
```text
!|1T285CHC7001      column 0, stream 1
!|1T0U71HCOW11      column 1, stream 1
!|1TN45CYO9N21      column 2, stream 1
!|1TI89OYNOW31      column 3, stream 1
```

requirements.heading: The Legacy Form - `1T` With Column/Stream Digits
requirements.text: N2_TITLE.RIP pairs `1T` with the 1.54 `1t` ([RIP_REGION_TEXT](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_region_text)) command instead of raw lines - `1t1…` lines carry justified text, with `1t0…` on each paragraph's final line (justify flag off), confirming the flowed text is fully justified within its column.

requirements.heading: Flowing Whole Files - `1R` on Plain Text
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWSPAPR.RIP, DRAGON.RIP, FONTS.RIP; STORY01.TXT, STORY02.TXT, DRAGON.TXT, FONTSTOR.TXT)._

requirements.heading: Flowing Whole Files - `1R` on Plain Text
requirements.text: Instead of inline raw lines, an open column set can be filled by `1R` ([RIP_READ_SCENE](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_read_scene)) pointed at a **plain prose file**:

requirements.heading: Flowing Whole Files - `1R` on Plain Text
Flowing Whole Files - `1R` on Plain Text
requirements.text: The named file (`STORY01.TXT` via the `$&…$` [dereference](5.0-host-commands.md)) is word-wrapped into the three open columns - it is **never parsed as RIPscrip**. The `.TXT` files in the corpus are ordinary paragraphs of prose, CRLF line ends, no introducers; the column system reflows them to fit. This split of _layout_ (the `.RIP`/`.COL` scene) from _copy_ (the `.TXT` file) is precisely a page-template system: change the story file, keep the layout. The `1R` target can equally be another variable, or an overflow page reference (next section).

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (DEMO-01.COL, NEWSPAPR.RIP)._

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: Text that does not fit the defined columns is not lost - it paginates into per-stream **overflow buffers**. The parameterized [text variable](../../glossary.md) `$OVERFLOW(…)$` (case-insensitive; the corpus writes it both ways) accesses them in two forms:

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | Form | Meaning |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | `$OVERFLOW(n,cur)$` | Stream _n_'s current page - used as a `1R` filename to flow that page into open columns |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | `$OVERFLOW(n,next)$` / `$OVERFLOW(n,prev)$` | Step stream _n_'s page pointer forward/back |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | `$OVERFLOW(n,page)$` | Expands to the current page number (a data variable) |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | optional `,setverbose` third argument | Observed only on the button forms - presumably enables end-of-pages feedback _(hypothesis)_ |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: | `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$` | Discard all overflow buffers - NEWSPAPR.RIP issues it under the comment "Reset all overflow files" before building the page |

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text: The pagination _loop_ is elegant: the pager scene re-plays **itself**. DEMO-01.COL's navigation fields step the pointer, then replay the very `.COL` template that re-reads the current page:

requirements.heading: Pagination - `$OVERFLOW$` and `$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`
requirements.text:
```text
!|1M00VWG0WUH01000000ID=6:$overflow(1,prev,setverbose)$$>demo-01.col$
!|1M00WUG0XUH01000000ID=7:$overflow(1,next,setverbose)$$>demo-01.col$
```

requirements.heading: The `.COL` Page Template - Worked Example
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (DEMO-01.COL, abridged)._

requirements.heading: The `.COL` Page Template - Worked Example
requirements.text: DEMO-01.COL is the complete pattern in one file: a reusable "continuation page" for stream 1 of the newspaper. Annotated and lightly abridged:

requirements.heading: The `.COL` Page Template - Worked Example
requirements.text:
```text
!|S010U|1K|W00|k00                                  Fill, kill old fields, write mode, back color
!|J10|n2000|M08|fZKQO                               Standard 3.x prologue: base 36, 2-byte
                                                    coords, 256-color mode, 1280x960 world
!|K8Y92IOQA                                         Page chrome: filled rectangles...
!|y00000G0S000000001a1a000000Marin                  Outline font for the folio line
!|@VAGQPage $overflow(1,page)$                      "Page N" counter
!|1M000G7Y8ICC1000000ID=2:$-=RETURN=>NEWSPAPR.RIP$$>TWEATHER.RIP$
!|1M000GCG8GGU1000000ID=3:$>N2_HORO.RIP$            Section navigation fields
!|1M00VWG0WUH01000000ID=6:$overflow(1,prev,setverbose)$$>demo-01.col$
!|1M00WUG0XUH01000000ID=7:$overflow(1,next,setverbose)$$>demo-01.col$
!|1M00XWG0YYH01000000ID=8:$>newspapr.rip$           Back to the front page
!|y0000000C000000001a1a000000dixon                  Body face: Dixon
!|1e4L3D919K0100010000000000                        Column 0, stream 1, overflow on
!|1e9L4SDF681100010000000000                        Column 1 - chained
!|1eDP4SHI5V2100010000000000                        Column 2 - chained
!|1R00000000$overflow(1,cur)$                       Flow the current overflow page in
!|1E                                                End of flowed text
!|1^[5000$MCURSOR(4)$                               Mouse-field entry/exit queries
!|1^[6000$MCURSOR(0)$
```

requirements.heading: The `.COL` Page Template - Worked Example
requirements.text: Every click on prev/next steps the stream pointer and replays this file; the file redraws the chrome, reopens the same three columns, and flows in whichever page is now current. DEMO-02.COL does the identical job for stream 2 (the secondary story).

requirements.heading: Drop Caps
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWS.RIP)._

requirements.heading: Drop Caps
requirements.text: NEWS.RIP demonstrates a typographic flourish the column system does not do natively - the author fakes it, instructively. A single oversized character is drawn at the first column's corner with plain `@` ([RIP_TEXT_XY](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_text_xy)) in a large Marin face, and the flowed article text simply **starts mid-word**:

requirements.heading: Drop Caps
requirements.text:
```text
!|y00003W0e040000001k1a000000Marin      Large display face
!|@A91Gª                                One extended-ASCII character (byte 0xAA) at the corner
!|y0000300U000000001k1a000000Marin      Back to the body size
wo years ago, TeleGrafix Communications stunned the computer industry with
```

requirements.heading: Drop Caps
requirements.text: The article reads "**T**wo years ago…" - the capital lives outside the flow, the byte `0xAA` presumably selecting an ornamental capital _T_ in the Marin outline font's extended range _(hypothesis)_. The flowed text wraps around nothing; the first column's region is simply drawn to start below/right of the cap.

requirements.heading: The Newspaper Demo - Showcase
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWSPAPR.RIP, N2_TITLE.RIP, N2_HORO.RIP, N2_BUSI.RIP, N2_PHOTO.RIP, TWEATHER.RIP, DEMO-01.COL, DEMO-02.COL, STORY01.TXT, STORY02.TXT)._

requirements.heading: The Newspaper Demo - Showcase
requirements.text: The system's full showcase is an **electronic newspaper**, and TeleGrafix built it as a customizable product, not a canned screen. NEWSPAPR.RIP opens with a configuration block under the comment _"Change these to the values you want for your content"_:

requirements.heading: The Newspaper Demo - Showcase
requirements.text:
```text
!|1^[0000$-=MAIN_STORY=story01.txt$|!     Filename containing main story
!|1^[0000$-=MAIN_AUTHOR=Jeff Reeder$|!    Author of main story
!|1^[0000$-=MAIN_TITLE=Rapid RIPscrip-3 Rocks The Net$
!|1^[0000$-=SUB_STORY=story02.txt$|!      Filename containing secondary story
```

requirements.heading: The Newspaper Demo - Showcase
requirements.text: The front page then draws a masthead in outline fonts, an "INSIDE" sidebar of four inline teaser columns (each an independent `1e` … `1E` block), the main headline as `@4L2L$&MAIN_TITLE$`, bylines as `By $&MAIN_AUTHOR$`, three chained columns flowing `$&MAIN_STORY$`, a boxed secondary story on stream 2 flowing `$&SUB_STORY$`, three captioned JPEG photographs (`1i`/`1p` - see [4.1 JPEG Images](4.1-jpeg-images.md)), and a navigation strip of mouse fields into the section pages - weather map, horoscopes (chained inline columns), business, and a JPEG photo gallery. Overflow from both stories pages into DEMO-01.COL and DEMO-02.COL. Swap two `.TXT` files and two title variables and it is _your_ newspaper - layout, pagination and navigation come free. Nothing else in the RIPscrip corpus, of any era, demonstrates this much of the 3.x design working together.

requirements.heading: Open Questions
requirements.text: _Evidence: corpus (NEWS.RIP); HLP; SyncTERM descriptor table._

requirements.heading: Open Questions
requirements.text:
- **`1A`** - a single occurrence (`!|1A010000`, NEWS.RIP) immediately before the flowed newspaper article; plausibly justification/hyphenation settings for the flow engine _(hypothesis)_. SyncTERM carries a descriptor-only entry for `1A` with seven words, which does not match the six digits observed.
- **`RIP_SelectArticle`** - present in the RIPSCRIP.HLP command-name inventory, and the obvious candidate for re-selecting a stream/article after the fact; its wire opcode never appears in the corpus. It almost certainly belongs to this article/column machinery _(hypothesis)_.
- RIPSCRIP.HLP error strings - "Invalid text article number", "Invalid text column number", and a wrap/chop designator for text windows - confirm the engine validates both identifiers and supports at least two flow modes.
- The `cc` field of the `1e` layout and the meaning of flag bits beyond bit 0 remain unknown; every corpus value is zero (and `0001`).

requirements.heading: 4.0 Icons & Bitmaps
requirements.text: _Reconstructed edition - every claim carries an evidence tag; see [Contents](README.md) for the legend._

requirements.heading: 4.0 Icons & Bitmaps
requirements.text: Raster imagery on the terminal: capturing screen regions to a [clipboard](../../glossary.md) port, pasting them back with logical put modes, loading and writing disk-based [icons](../../glossary.md), and the block-move commands. Under the 2.0 engine that 3.x inherits, icons are Windows **BMP** bitmaps - `.BMP` for icons, `.BMH` for [hot icons](../../glossary.md), `.BMM` for [icon masks](../../glossary.md) - replacing the 1.54 `.ICN`/`.HIC`/`.MSK` formats.

requirements.heading: 4.0 Icons & Bitmaps
requirements.text: _The 1.54 record is [4.0 in the v1.54 reference](../../1.54/ripscrip/4.0-images-and-icons.md); the 2.0 record is [4.0 in the v2.0 reference](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md). Byte-level format is in the [v2.0 icon formats techspec](../../2.0/techspecs/3.0-icon-formats.md), unchanged in 3.x, with the RIPtel file census in the [binary-formats research](../../3.0/research/riptel-binary-formats.md)._

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: _Copy rectangular image to the clipboard port_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `C`                             |

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:XY y0:XY x1:XY y1:XY res:1` |

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1C <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <res>` **Example:** `!|1CEM6XFZ7U0`

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_get_image)) · HLP (`RIP_GetImage`; clipboard port concept, `$SCB$`/`$RCB$`/`$P$` variables) · corpus (4 uses in LANDSCPE.RIP) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:15847)

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: This command instructs the terminal program to copy a rectangular region defined by (x0,y0) to (x1,y1) in the currently active drawing port to the first offscreen port found after port #0 (the screen port). If no offscreen port is actually found, then the first empty port slot is used; the slot is defined as an offscreen bitmap port and is initialized to the dimensions of the source rectangle used in this command. If an offscreen bitmap port is found, then it is deleted and re-initialized based on the dimensions of this command. Once the offscreen bitmap port is initialized, the contents of the source rectangle are copied to the port, occupying the entire contents of the port. If the port number that is found corresponds to the source port, then this command does nothing. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: In older versions of RIPscrip (v1.54 and earlier), there was only the screen and one offscreen bitmap port (the clipboard). Under the 2.0/3.x engine, you may have multiple offscreen bitmap ports (or clipboards). There are three commands from RIPscrip 1.54 that pertain directly to the concept of a clipboard (RIP*GET_IMAGE, [RIP_PUT_IMAGE](#rip_put_image) and [RIP_WRITE_ICON](#rip_write_icon)). To facilitate the integration of these commands in the newer architecture, a clipboard pointer is used. The clipboard pointer is created when the RIP_GET_IMAGE command is used. When this command is executed, the software will scan from port #1 to port #35 (port #0 is skipped because it's the screen). It searches for the first open (unused) port. Once found, the clipboard pointer is set to point to this port. This allows the RIP_PUT_IMAGE and RIP_WRITE_ICON command to know which port number is associated with the clipboard. *(v2.A3)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: When a [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) command is executed, the contents of the port table are cleared and the clipboard pointer is cleared (ie, no clipboard exists after the operation is complete). _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: If the offscreen port cannot be defined for whatever reason, then this command is not processed. The only thing that will be accomplished in this case is that the clipboard pointer will be cleared and no clipboard data will exist. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: See the [RIP_DEFINE_PORT](7.0-drawing-ports.md#rip_define_port) command for more details about offscreen ports and the size limitations of them. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_GET_IMAGE
requirements.text: In the corpus, LANDSCPE.RIP grabs small texture tiles this way for re-stamping with [RIP_PUT_IMAGE](#rip_put_image); for port-addressed copies the 3.x demos overwhelmingly prefer the level-2 [RIP_PORT_COPY](7.0-drawing-ports.md#rip_port_copy). _Evidence: corpus (LANDSCPE.RIP)._

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: _Pastes the clipboard port's contents to another port_

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `P`                      |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x:XY y:XY mode:2 res:1` |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1P <x> <y> <mode> <res>` **Example:** `!|1PV4OM000`

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_put_image)) · HLP (`RIP_PutImage`; `$P$` paste-clipboard variable) · corpus (1 use in NEWSPAPR.RIP) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16481)

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: This command takes the contents of the port identified by the clipboard pointer (see the [RIP_GET_IMAGE](#rip_get_image) command above) and copies it to a position (x,y) in the currently active drawing port. If the two ports refer to the same port number, then this command is ignored. If the clipboard pointer is clear (ie, no clipboard port is in use), then this command is also ignored. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: The area in the active drawing port that is overwritten with the graphics data is determined by the dimensions of the clipboard port previously established with a RIP*GET_IMAGE function. *(v2.A3)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: The position on the active drawing port that is to receive the image is specified by the (x,y) parameters. These define the upper left corner that will be the rectangle to receive the image data. If any part of the image would go off the edge of the viewport (or the screen) then it is truncated appropriately. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: The image that is retrieved from the clipboard port does so based on the port's viewport (the entire contents of the viewport are copied to the active drawing port). If the clipboard port is only used with the RIP*GET_IMAGE command, then the viewport will be the full size of the port. If however, some port related commands are used on this clipboard port, then it is possible to alter the viewport inside this port. This gives you the ability to paste sub-areas of the port's actual image onto the destination drawing port. *(v2.A3)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: The `<mode>` parameter defines "how" the image will be pasted on the active drawing port:

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | Mode | Description                                          | Logical |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | 00   | Paste the image on-screen normally                   | (COPY)  |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | 01   | Exclusive-OR image with the one already in the port  | (XOR)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | 02   | Logically OR image with the one already in the port  | (OR)    |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | 03   | Logically AND image with the one already in the port | (AND)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: | 04   | Paste the inverse of the image in the port           | (NOT)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: NOTE: The 1-byte `<res>` parameter is RESERVED FOR FUTURE USE and should be set to zero.

requirements.heading: RIP_PUT_IMAGE
requirements.text: Its single corpus appearance re-stamps a captured screen region in the newspaper demo; everywhere else the demos use the more general [RIP_PORT_COPY](7.0-drawing-ports.md#rip_port_copy). _Evidence: corpus (NEWSPAPR.RIP)._

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: _Write contents of the clipboard port to disk_

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `W`              |

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `res:1 filename` |

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1W <res> <filename>` **Example:** `!|1W0filename.icn`

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_write_icon)) · HLP (`RIP_WriteIcon`) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16969) - not observed in the RIPtel demo corpus

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: This command takes the contents of the clipboard port and writes it to disk as a BMP type bitmap file. The image written to disk is the image contained inside the viewport of the clipboard port (see the [RIP_PUT_IMAGE](#rip_put_image) command for more details about viewports and the clipboard port). If the clipboard pointer indicates that there is no clipboard in use, then this command does nothing. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: Once the file is written to disk, you may subsequently use the [RIP_LOAD_ICON](#rip_load_icon) or [RIP_LOAD_BITMAP](#rip_load_bitmap) commands to load the icon back onto a drawing port. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: Path or sub-directory information is not allowed in the filename portion of the command. If an Icon by the same name already exists on disk, it is overwritten. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: NOTE: The `<res>` parameter is reserved for future use by TeleGrafix. For future compatibility, it should be set to "0". _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_WRITE_ICON
requirements.text: The demos keep their snapshots in offscreen ports instead of round-tripping through disk, so the command never appears in the corpus. _Evidence: corpus (absence)._

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: _Loads and displays a disk-based icon to current port_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `I`                                                   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x:XY y:XY mode:2 clipboard:1 scale:1 res:1 filename` |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1I <x> <y> <mode> <clipboard> <scale> <res> <filename>` **Example:** `!|1I001101010button`

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_load_icon)) · HLP (`RIP_LoadIcon`; plus 1.54-compat strings "Can't convert RIP 1.54 Icon %s to 2.0 BMP format!") · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16302) - not observed in the RIPtel demo corpus

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: This command instructs the terminal to read an icon from disk and display it at the given upper-left (x,y) location in the current drawing port. If the width or height of the Icon would make it go off the right or left edge of the port's viewport, it will be truncated to fit inside the viewport. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The `<mode>` parameter defines the modes in which the Icon will be displayed on the current drawing port. The modes are identical to the [RIP_PUT_IMAGE](#rip_put_image) command, and are as follows:

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The .BMP file extension does not need to be included as part of the filename. If omitted, it will automatically be appended to the filename. If an extension is provided, it will be used verbatim. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | Mode | Description                                        | Logical |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 00   | Paste the image on-screen normally                 | (COPY)  |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 01   | Exclusive-OR image with the one already on screen  | (XOR)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 02   | Logically OR image with the one already on screen  | (OR)    |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 03   | Logically AND image with the one already on screen | (AND)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 04   | Paste the inverse of the image on the screen       | (NOT)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The `<clipboard>` parameter can be one of two values: _(v2.A2)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | Value | Description                                                 |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 0     | Load the image onto the port verbatim                       |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: | 1     | Load the image onto the port and put it onto clipboard port |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: If the `<clipboard>` parameter specifies to put the icon's image onto a clipboard port, the order of operation is the following: _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text:
1. The image is loaded onto the current drawing port, truncated to the viewport if necessary.
2. A [RIP_GET_IMAGE](#rip_get_image) command is performed transparently to copy the resultant image in the current drawing port onto the clipboard port (it will be defined if necessary, otherwise it will be re-defined). If the clipboard port is the same port as the current drawing port, then this phase is omitted. The rectangle copied to the clipboard port is based on the resultant, possibly truncated image.

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The `<scale>` parameter indicates whether the icon should be scaled to the device coordinates when it is loaded. A `1` indicates that it should be scaled, and a `0` indicates that it not should be scaled. This is important when dealing with older RIPscrip 1.54 icons. Icons that are loaded with RIPscrip 1.54 need to be resolution independent. This is performed when this command has a 1 in the scale parameter's position. All scaling is performed in this command as if the icon were created in a 640x350 environment. So, if an icon is loaded that is 35 pixels tall, and it is displayed in a 640x480 environment, it will be stretched vertically to make it 48 pixels tall. This makes sure that icons loaded in this mode are displayed at the correct size so that they are resolution independent. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: NOTE: By default this value must be set to `1` (scaled)! _(v2.A2)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The `<filename>` parameter must not contain any sub-directory or path information and must specify a valid Icon file name. If the Icon cannot be located or an error occurs on the disk, then a box should be displayed on screen indicating that the given Icon File could not be loaded. If this happens, then no clipboard operations are performed - except that the clipboard is cleared and the clipboard pointer is cleared as well. This visual prompt indicates that something is amiss to the end-user. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: NOTE: The `<res>` parameter is reserved for future use by TeleGrafix Communications, Inc.. It should be set to 0 for compatibility with future releases. _(v2.A2)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_ICON
requirements.text: The 3.0 driver retains this 1.54-lineage icon stamper chiefly for backward compatibility - HLP shows built-in `.ICN`→BMP conversion (below) - but the corpus ships no `.ICN` files at all and always uses [RIP_LOAD_BITMAP](#rip_load_bitmap). _Evidence: HLP; corpus (absence)._

requirements.heading: Legacy `.ICN` icons and on-the-fly conversion
requirements.text: The 1.54 icon format - Borland `getimage()` memory dumps, documented in the [v1.54 reference](../../1.54/ripscrip/6.1-content-file-roles.md) - is not a native 3.x format, but the 3.0 driver retains read support by _converting_ legacy icons to BMP on the fly: the DLL exports `RIP_ConvertIconToBmp` and carries the error strings "Can't convert RIP 1.54 Icon %s to 2.0 BMP format!" and "1.54 icon file %s has an invalid width". No `.ICN` files ship with RIPtel; hosts are expected to serve BMPs. See [6.1 Content File Roles](6.1-content-file-roles.md#legacy-icn-icons-ripscrip-154) for the file-role view of the same behavior.

requirements.heading: Legacy `.ICN` icons and on-the-fly conversion
requirements.text: _Evidence: HLP (RIPSCRIP.HLP error strings; RIPTEL.EXE export table)._

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: _Loads and displays a disk-based bitmap to screen_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | **Command** | `b` |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:XY y0:XY x1:XY y1:XY duplicate_port:1 mode:1 flags:2 trans_color:2 res:4 filename` |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1b <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <duplicate_port> <mode> <flags> <trans_color> <res> <filename>` **Example:** `!|1b0000HS0Y000G000000STRIP6.BMP`

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_load_bitmap)) · HLP (`RIP_LoadBitmap`; also the `$<FILE.BMP$` macro shorthand) · corpus (69 uses in 28 files) - not in SyncTERM

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: This command is nearly identical in nature to the [RIP_LOAD_ICON](#rip_load_icon) command but it is more flexible in that it supports arbitrary scaling of the bitmap to the destination screen and it supports dithering methods. It can be made to exactly match the RIP*LOAD_ICON command. *(v2.A1)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: This command instructs the terminal to read a bitmap from disk and display it at the given upper-left (x0,y0) location. If the (x1,y1) values are non-zero, then it specifies the lower-right corner on the screen for the bitmap's display region. If the bitmap differs in size than the destination rectangle, then it is scaled (stretched) to fit into the proper region. If the values of X1 and Y1 are zero, then the bitmap is shown verbatim in whatever resolution of the disk based file (this is more like the RIP*LOAD_ICON command above). *(v2.A3)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: The .BMP file extension does not need to be included as part of the filename. If omitted, it will automatically be appended to the filename. If an extension is provided, it will be used verbatim. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: If the width or height of the Icon would make it go off the right or bottom edge of the viewport, the bitmap will be clipped. The `<mode>` parameter defines the modes in which the Icon will be displayed on the screen. The modes are identical to the [RIP_PUT_IMAGE](#rip_put_image) and the RIP*LOAD_ICON commands, and are as follows: *(v2.A1)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | Mode | Description                                      | Logical |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | 0    | Paste the image onto the port normally           | (COPY)  |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | 1    | Exclusive-OR image with one already on the port  | (XOR)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | 2    | Logically OR image with one already on the port  | (OR)    |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | 3    | Logically AND image with one already on the port | (AND)   |

requirements.heading: RIP_LOAD_BITMAP
requirements.text: | 4    | Paste the inverse of the image onto the port     | (NOT)   |

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: The `<flags>` parameter contains important bit-field values that can be OR'd together to produce a number of desired operations. The possible flag values are:

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: **Flag 1** - Load the image onto the port and make a copy to another port. This is used to make a carbon copy of the image once it is placed onto the active drawing port. This means that after any color palette manipulation, dithering and viewport clipping, the final image is copied to some other drawing port as a type of backup copy. This is often used to make high-speed copies of the same image without having to continually access the disk in order to load the image over and over again. If this flag is specified, then the `<duplicate_port>` parameter determines which port number will receive the loaded image. If you specify a value of 0 for the duplicate port number, then it will act like the RIP*LOAD_ICON command's clipboard mode - it loads the image onto the clipboard port specified by the clipboard pointer, or if the pointer hasn't been used yet, then it places the image on a newly created offscreen bitmap port located in the first unused port number. The offscreen port will be redefined with the new bitmap's dimensions. If the `<duplicate_port>` parameter specifies a value from 1-35, then it indicates a specific port number. That port, if it doesn't exist, will be defined as an offscreen bitmap port with the exact same dimensions as the final bitmap. If it does exist, then the port is deleted (even if it's a screen-port) and redefined as an offscreen bitmap port with the new bitmap's dimensions. After the duplicate port is defined, the image is copied to it. If the current drawing port happens to be the same port used for the duplicate port, then this flag is ignored. If this flag is omitted, then no duplicate copy is made of the image and the `<duplicate_port>` parameter of this command is ignored. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: **Flag 2** - This flag indicates to take the color palette in the bitmap file and activate it in the current color lookup table. This means that the color palette in the bitmap is copied into the video device's color palette (and into RIPscrip's). This means that if any graphics are already on the screen when this happens, they might change in color as soon as the bitmap is loaded (this is due to the fact that the color palette is changed). If the number of colors in the bitmap exceeds the number of colors in the active display device, then the actual color palette in use is used for the bitmap instead of the internal bitmap palette. If the number of colors in the bitmap is equal or less than the number of colors for the active video mode then the image will be displayed exactly as it was intended. If this is the case, then no dithering is necessary on the image so the dither flag (see below) parameter is ignored. If the terminal is running in a mode that doesn't allow for a color palette in the video hardware, then dithering is ignored and the color palette inside the bitmap file is ignored - this is because the system is already running in a 32K, 64K or 24-bit color mode and there are more than plenty colors to represent the bitmap perfectly. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: If this flag is omitted, then the bitmap will use the current screen's color palette. Typically this will be the default color palette for use with RIPscrip but it might be different. This means that any pixel of the bitmap that is drawn to the screen is shown in whatever actual color is the absolute closest to the color palette number corresponding to that pixel in the bitmap (dithering may still apply - see below). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: If the bitmap has no color palette (eg, 24-bit bitmaps), then this flag is ignored. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: **Flag 4** - This flag enables auto-dithering mode. This is an intelligent way of determining if dithering should be performed or not. If there are more colors in the bitmap than in the video device or if the bitmap's color palette is not used to set the video device, then dithering is used to get the image as close to the original color scheme as possible. If the bitmap's palette is committed to the video device then no dithering is necessary because the color palette in use has all (or more) of the necessary colors to display the image. 24-bit images will always enable dithering if this mode is used unless the terminal is running in 24-bit mode. Dithering slows down image drawing so it should only be used for images that really need it. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: If this flag is omitted, then no dither is performed at all. If the number of colors in the bitmap is higher than the number of colors in the display device then this will yield a lower quality image. But if there are more colors in the display device than the bitmap then the quality of the image will be close to the actual bitmap (or exact). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: **Flag 8** - Place the bitmap image onto the screen with one of its colors "transparent". This means that the color index specified in the `<trans_color>` parameter will be treated as a transparent color. This color will "show through" to whatever graphics were behind the bitmap. This applies to all forms of bitmaps (monochrome through 24-bit). With bitmaps that have no palette, then only colors in the 24-bit range that "map" to this particular transparent color will actually appear as transparent. When used in combination with dithering (when dithering is performed), transparent regions could be "grainy" in appearance due to the dithering process. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: If the bitmap is placed onto a duplicate port, then it is done in a specific order. The image is shown on the current drawing port (with possible transparency) then the resulting image (after color palette translation and dithering are performed) is placed onto the duplicate port. This is done so that the image in the duplicate port will already have its processing done on it so that subsequent duplicate operations will not require any color translation or dithering (a speed consideration). If transparency mode is used, then the image duplicated includes any graphics "behind" the image that show through in the transparent locations. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: The `<filename>` parameter must not contain any sub-directory or path information and must specify a valid bitmap file name. If the bitmap cannot be located or an error occurs on the disk, then a box should be displayed on screen indicating that the given bitmap could not be loaded. This visual prompt indicates that something is amiss to the end-user. The size of the box will be as big as the destination bitmap image on screen. If the X1 and Y1 are zero, then some suitable box should be drawn. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: NOTE: The 4-byte `<res>` parameter is RESERVED FOR THE FUTURE and should be set to "0000". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: A host command can also stamp a bitmap via the `$<file.BMP$` playback prefix - see [5.3 Local File Playback](5.3-local-playback.md#local-bitmap-playback---filebmp).

requirements.heading: Bitmap Flags
requirements.text: The scaling, dithering, transparency-capable bitmap loader (added v2.A1) that superseded [RIP_LOAD_ICON](#rip_load_icon). The corpus uses it constantly: the example (DRAGON.RIP) stretches STRIP6.BMP across a 640×34 header band; DBACK.FN stamps TORCH.BMP with flag 8 + `trans_color` for transparent-color compositing; menu scenes place TELBUT.BMP button skins with `(x1,y1)` zero for verbatim size. HLP notes the driver "Can't show compressed bitmaps" - RLE-compressed and OS/2-style BMPs are unsupported ([6.1](6.1-content-file-roles.md#windows-bmp--dib)). _Evidence: HLP; corpus (DRAGON.RIP, DBACK.FN, TELDEMOS.MNU and others)._

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: _Copy a screen area to a new location (bit blit)_

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `g`                                            |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:2 y0:2 x1:2 y1:2 dx0:2 dy0:2 mode:1 res:1` |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Draw Color, Back Color, Fill Style, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_copy_blit)) · HLP (`RIP_CopyBlit`) · corpus (88 uses in 6 files) - not in SyncTERM

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: This command is similar to the [RIP_SCROLL](#rip_scroll) command but is more generic in nature - it can move a rectangle of graphical information on the screen from one position to another - not just up or down. It does this with high-speed bit-blit operations. The rectangle contained in (x0,y0) to (x1,y1) is copied so that its upper-left corner is now at the location (dx0,dy0).

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: Some, part, or none of the original source image might be covered up by the moved screen data. The parts of the original image which are still on the screen (unobscured) can be cleared to some color or state if you wish by using the `<mode>` parameter (like RIP_SCROLL does). The possible settings for `<mode>` are:

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | Mode | Description |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 0 | Do nothing - leave the old graphics on the screen |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 1 | Fill the old graphical area with the current drawing color (solid fill in COPY mode). |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 2 | Fill the old graphical area with the current background drawing color (solid fill in COPY mode). |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 3 | Fill the area with the current fill color (solid fill in COPY mode). Fill pattern/styles are not used for this. |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 4 | Fill the old graphical area with the current fill style/pattern in the current fill color. |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: | 5 | Erase the affected area entirely to black. |

requirements.heading: RIP_COPY_BLIT
requirements.text: The corpus uses it as a _within-screen_ slide primitive in the wipe/transition library (WIPE00-02.FN, DL.FN, DR.FN): the example shifts a 1080×960-wide slab 72 world-units right in one step of a push transition. _Evidence: corpus (WIPE00.FN, WIPE01.FN, WIPE02.FN, DL.FN, DR.FN)._

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: _This command was formerly RIP_COPY_REGION._

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: _Copy (scroll) screen region up/down_

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `G`                                                |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:XY y0:XY x1:XY y1:XY mode:1 res:1 dest_line:2` |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1G <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <mode> <res> <dest_line>` **Example:** `!|1G080G140M0005`

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.0-icons-and-bitmaps.md#rip_scroll)) · HLP (`RIP_Scroll`) · SyncTERM (ripper.c:16246 - **documentation-only stub**: full 1.54 spec comment, then a bare `break;`) - not observed in the RIPtel demo corpus

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: This command physically "copies" a rectangular region of the graphics screen up or down. The `<dest_line>` parameter is the Y position that is the destination scan line to receive the region. The Destination of the copy can overlap the original region, but cannot be on the same line. You cannot move the image area left or right at all. This command is designated for vertical scrolling of graphical data either up or down.

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: This is one of the only graphical output commands that DOES NOT adhere to the [RIP_VIEWPORT](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_viewport) command. In other words, you can scroll graphical data outside the current graphical viewport (even over the text window!). However, it does adhere to the boundaries of the current drawing port. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: The `<mode>` parameter instructs the terminal what to do with the part of the source rectangle that isn't covered up by the scrolled data. You may specify several things to happen as defined by the mode values below: _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | Mode | Description |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 0 | Do nothing - leave the old graphics on the screen |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 1 | Fill the old graphical area with the current drawing color (solid fill in COPY mode). |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 2 | Fill the old graphical area with the current background drawing color (solid fill in COPY mode). |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 3 | Fill the area with the current fill color (solid fill in COPY mode). Fill pattern/styles are not used for this. |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 4 | Fill the old graphical area with the current fill style/pattern in the current fill color. |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 5 | Erase the affected area entirely to black. |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: | 6 | Fill the affected area with the color of a pixel from one of the corners of the affected rectangle. If the image area was scrolled up, then the color is taken from the lower-right most pixel from the old graphical rectangle (left exposed). If the data is scrolled down, then the rectangle is filled in with the color of the pixel in the upper-left most pixel. This is mode is used so that if the area is a multi-colored graphic, that a suitable fill color is used. |

requirements.heading: RIP_SCROLL
requirements.text: It is the one command SyncTERM documents in-source but does not implement - recognized and swallowed. The corpus does all of its region moving with [RIP_COPY_BLIT](#rip_copy_blit) and level-2 [RIP_PORT_COPY](7.0-drawing-ports.md#rip_port_copy) instead. _Evidence: SyncTERM (ripper.c:16246); corpus (absence)._

requirements.heading: Masks and transparency
requirements.text: The 1.54 technique of stamping a mask icon in AND mode and the image in OR mode still works with the put modes above, and the `.BMM` mask extension exists for that role (see [6.1 Content File Roles](6.1-content-file-roles.md#file-roles) - no `.BMM` files are known to have shipped, and the 3.x record adds no sighting). The preferred route since 2.0 is [RIP_LOAD_BITMAP](#rip_load_bitmap)'s transparency flag (flag 8 with `<trans_color>`), which makes one color of the bitmap show through to the graphics behind it in a single operation - exactly how the corpus composites its torch and décor art (DBACK.FN).

requirements.heading: Masks and transparency
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4; corpus (DBACK.FN)._

requirements.heading: 4.1 JPEG Images
requirements.text: _Reconstructed edition - every claim carries an evidence tag; see [Contents](README.md) for the legend._

requirements.heading: 4.1 JPEG Images
requirements.text: Photographic images - a capability of the 2.0/3.x generation with no 1.54 counterpart: a host delivers a compressed image file to the terminal and displays it scaled into an **image area**, a sub-region of the current viewport established by [RIP_IMAGE_STYLE](#rip_image_style). JPEG is the only compressed image format in shipping 3.x - the ALPHA 4 draft also added GIF _(v2.A4)_, but GIF was dropped over LZW licensing before shipping, and PNG was announced but never shipped (see the [white paper](../text/RIPScrip-3.x-technical-whitepaper.txt)) - and SyncTERM's `RIPSCRIP030001` mode has no raster support at all, making JPEG display a clean 3.x-only differentiator.

requirements.heading: 4.1 JPEG Images
requirements.text: _Evidence: WP (§3.7.2, GrayPEG); HLP (jpeg\_ strings; readme progressive-display note); corpus (7 shipped JPEGs, 16 references)._

requirements.heading: 4.1 JPEG Images
requirements.text: _The 2.0 record is [4.1 in the v2.0 reference](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.1-jpeg-images.md); decoder profile, scaling and palette-rendering internals are in the [v2.0 JPEG techspec](../../2.0/techspecs/3.1-jpeg-images.md), and the file-role view is [6.1 Content File Roles](6.1-content-file-roles.md#jpeg-and-graypeg)._

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: _Display a scalable photo type image_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `p`              |

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `res:4 filename` |

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Format:** `!|1p <res> <filename>` **Example:** `!|1p0000ASTRO.JPG`

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Write Mode, Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.1-jpeg-images.md#rip_image)) · HLP (`RIP_Image`; JPEG engine strings - jpegShow, LoadJPEGBuffer; the `$(FILE.JPG$` macro) · corpus (13 uses in 6 files, 16 JPEG references) - not in SyncTERM

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: This command will physically take a JPEG image file that is located on the remote terminal's hard disk (like Icon files) and display it in the image area set by a [RIP_IMAGE_STYLE](#rip_image_style) command. See the RIP*IMAGE_STYLE command for more details on the options available to set for image viewing and manipulation. *(v2.A0)\_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: Display can also be triggered by receiving an image via [RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_enter_block_mode) with an image file type, or by the `$(file.JPG$` playback prefix in a host command ([5.3 Local File Playback](5.3-local-playback.md#local-jpeg-playback---filejpg)). A host can confirm JPEG capability first with [`$IFS(JPEG)$`](5.1-text-variables.md#ifs).

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: All JPEGs are 24-bit; the white paper notes support for the **GrayPEG** grayscale variants, and progressive ("display while downloading") rendering was advertised but noted as not working in RIPtel 3.1. _Evidence: WP (§3.7.2, GrayPEG); HLP (readme progressive-display note)._

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: The corpus's photo scenes (N2_PHOTO.RIP, N2_TITLE.RIP, IMAGES.RIP, FXSHWIMG.FN) cycle ASTRO/GALAXY/JUPITER/BEACH2/BRIDGE02/DUSK_SEA/FIRCLOUD JPEGs. SPECLEFX.RIP demonstrates the conditional slideshow idiom, the filename argument computed by the [macro layer](5.2-templates-and-conditionals.md) at execution time:

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text:
```text
!|1p0000<<IF $INUSE(TV,NEXT_IMG)$="0">>$-=NEXT_IMG=ASTRO.JPG$<<ENDIF>>$&NEXT_IMG$
```

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE
requirements.text: - if the `NEXT_IMG` variable is unset, initialize it, then display whatever it dereferences to. FXSHWIMG.FN brackets its slow JPEG display with [RIP_SET_MOUSE_CURSOR](4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#rip_set_mouse_cursor) hourglass/arrow switches. _Evidence: corpus (SPECLEFX.RIP, FXSHWIMG.FN)._

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: _Alter subsequent displayed image settings_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: | **Command**   | `i`                                      |

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: | **Arguments** | `x0:XY y0:XY x1:XY y1:XY flags:4 res:12` |

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: **Attributes used:** Viewport, Port, Base Math (current setting) **Evidence:** 2.00a4 ([2.0 entry](../../2.0/ripscrip/4.1-jpeg-images.md#rip_image_style)) · HLP (`RIP_ImageStyle`; also the `$IMGSTYLE(cur,x0,y0,x1,y1)$` variable) · corpus (13 uses in 6 files) - not in SyncTERM

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: This command alters the settings for subsequently received (or displayed) image files. RIPscrip supports the display of JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) files. These files can be transmitted to the remote terminal and viewed. The `<x0>`, `<y0>`, `<x1>` and `<y1>` parameters determine the size of the image area in the current viewport. _(v2.A0)_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: If the `<x0>`, `<y0>`, `<x1>` and `<y1>` parameters are all set to zero (0), then Image Viewing is disabled. Any explicitly viewed images, or any images received with [RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_enter_block_mode) will be ignored (however they will be deleted if flag 4 or 8 are active - see below). _(v2.A0)_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: If the image view area is larger than the current viewport size, then the image area size will be adjusted according to the viewport's current size to fit. _(v2.A0)_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: The image will be scaled to fit inside the specified display region. If any of these coordinates extend beyond the dimensions of the viewport, they will be adjusted to fit. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: There is a `<flags>` parameter which alters some of the aspects of the image being displayed. These flags can be OR'd together to create a combination of various flag values. The possible flags are: _(v2.A0)_

requirements.heading: RIP_IMAGE_STYLE
requirements.text: | Value | Description |
