requirements.heading: Date and Time Text Variables
requirements.text: These text variables return information on the current date and/or the current time. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Date and Time Text Variables
requirements.text: The full 1.54/2.00a4 date and time group survives intact in 3.x - all thirteen date variables and all seven time variables are in the HLP table and in SyncTERM's `rv_date`/`rv_time` handler groups. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8061 `rv_date`; 8148 `rv_time`)._

requirements.heading: $ADOW$
requirements.text: _Abbreviated Day of Week_

requirements.heading: $ADOW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ADOW$` **Syntax:** `$ADOW$`

requirements.heading: $ADOW$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current day of the week in abbreviated form. Possible values are: Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri and Sat.

requirements.heading: $ADOW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ADOW$` **Returns:** `Mon`

requirements.heading: $AMPM$
requirements.text: _Returns AM or PM depending on time_

requirements.heading: $AMPM$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$AMPM$` **Syntax:** `$AMPM$`

requirements.heading: $AMPM$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a two-character value of either "AM" or "PM" depending on what time it is.

requirements.heading: $AMPM$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$AMPM$` **Returns:** `PM`

requirements.heading: $DATE$
requirements.text: _Date in short format_

requirements.heading: $DATE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DATE$` **Syntax:** `$DATE$`

requirements.heading: $DATE$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current date. in the format MM/DD/YY.

requirements.heading: $DATE$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DATE$` **Returns:** `12/19/93`

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text: _Date and Time_

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DATETIME$` **Syntax:** `$DATETIME$`

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a combination date and time. The format is somewhat different than standard time/date notation. It is:

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text:
```text
DAY-OF-WEEK   MONTH   DAY-OF-MONTH  HH:MM:SS  YEAR
```

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DATETIME$` **Returns:** `Sat Dec 19 14:38:50 1993`

requirements.heading: $DATETIME$
requirements.text: > NOTE: This is the standard Unix date/time notation.

requirements.heading: $DAY$
requirements.text: _Day of Month Number_

requirements.heading: $DAY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DAY$` **Syntax:** `$DAY$`

requirements.heading: $DAY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current day of the month. Possible values for this Variable are from 01-31.

requirements.heading: $DAY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DAY$` **Returns:** `05`

requirements.heading: $DOW$
requirements.text: _Day of week fully spelled out_

requirements.heading: $DOW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DOW$` **Syntax:** `$DOW$`

requirements.heading: $DOW$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current day of the week. The name is fully spelled out. Possible values are: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday.

requirements.heading: $DOW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DOW$` **Returns:** `Saturday`

requirements.heading: $DOY$
requirements.text: _Day of year_

requirements.heading: $DOY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DOY$` **Syntax:** `$DOY$`

requirements.heading: $DOY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the number of days so far in the year. A year has 365 days (except leap years which have 366). `$DOY$` can return 001 - 366.

requirements.heading: $DOY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DOY$` **Returns:** `214`

requirements.heading: $FYEAR$
requirements.text: _4 digit year_

requirements.heading: $FYEAR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$FYEAR$` **Syntax:** `$FYEAR$`

requirements.heading: $FYEAR$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the four-digit number of the current year.

requirements.heading: $FYEAR$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$FYEAR$` **Returns:** `1993`

requirements.heading: $HOUR$
requirements.text: _Hour (format HH) - normal style_

requirements.heading: $HOUR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$HOUR$` **Syntax:** `$HOUR$`

requirements.heading: $HOUR$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the two digit number of the current hour. This variable range from 01 - 12. This does not use military format.

requirements.heading: $HOUR$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$HOUR$` **Returns:** `11`

requirements.heading: $MHOUR$
requirements.text: _Hour (format HH) - military style_

requirements.heading: $MHOUR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MHOUR$` **Syntax:** `$MHOUR$`

requirements.heading: $MHOUR$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a two-digit number of the current hour in military format. This variable may range from 00 - 23.

requirements.heading: $MHOUR$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MHOUR$` **Returns:** `17`

requirements.heading: $MIN$
requirements.text: _Minutes_

requirements.heading: $MIN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MIN$` **Syntax:** `$MIN$`

requirements.heading: $MIN$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the two-digit number representing the current minutes in the hour. Possible values for this variable are 00-59.

requirements.heading: $MIN$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MIN$` **Returns:** `45`

requirements.heading: $MONTH$
requirements.text: _Month Name_

requirements.heading: $MONTH$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MONTH$` **Syntax:** `$MONTH$`

requirements.heading: $MONTH$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the full name of the current month. It is not abbreviated (e.g., "November" instead of "Nov")

requirements.heading: $MONTH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MONTH$` **Returns:** `December`

requirements.heading: $MONTHNUM$
requirements.text: _Month Number_

requirements.heading: $MONTHNUM$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MONTHNUM$` **Syntax:** `$MONTHNUM$`

requirements.heading: $MONTHNUM$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the number of the current month. January=01 and December=12.

requirements.heading: $MONTHNUM$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MONTHNUM$` **Returns:** `12`

requirements.heading: $SEC$
requirements.text: _Seconds_

requirements.heading: $SEC$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$SEC$` **Syntax:** `$SEC$`

requirements.heading: $SEC$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a 2-digit number representing the current seconds of the minute. Possible values for this variable are 00-59.

requirements.heading: $SEC$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$SEC$` **Returns:** `59`

requirements.heading: $TIME$
requirements.text: _Time in standard format_

requirements.heading: $TIME$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TIME$` **Syntax:** `$TIME$`

requirements.heading: $TIME$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the time in military format (hours from 00 - 23). The format is hours, minutes, and seconds separated by colons. HH:MM:SS

requirements.heading: $TIME$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TIME$` **Returns:** `18:09:33`

requirements.heading: $TIMEZONE$
requirements.text: _Time Zone or "NONE" if unknown_

requirements.heading: $TIMEZONE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TIMEZONE$` **Syntax:** `$TIMEZONE$`

requirements.heading: $TIMEZONE$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a word/phrase that describes the time-zone the terminal is in. This may be returned as anything like "PST" for Pacific Standard Time, "EST" for Eastern Standard Time, etc. If the time zone is not set on your PC, this variable will respond with NONE

requirements.heading: $TIMEZONE$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TIMEZONE$` **Returns:** `PST`

requirements.heading: $WDAY$
requirements.text: _Day of Week_

requirements.heading: $WDAY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$WDAY$` **Syntax:** `$WDAY$`

requirements.heading: $WDAY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a one-digit number representing the day of the week. Possible values are 0-6, where 0=Sunday (the first day in the week).

requirements.heading: $WDAY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$WDAY$` **Returns:** `2`

requirements.heading: $WOY$
requirements.text: _Week of current year 00-53; Sunday=1st Day of Week_

requirements.heading: $WOY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$WOY$` **Syntax:** `$WOY$`

requirements.heading: $WOY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a number from 00-53, representing the week in the year. Even though there are 52 weeks in a year, a week might not begin exactly on the first day of the year, so a maximum value for this variable can be 53 under these circumstances. For this variable, Sunday is considered to be the first day of the week.

requirements.heading: $WOY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$WOY$` **Returns:** `32`

requirements.heading: $WOYM$
requirements.text: _Week of current year 00-53; Monday=1st Day of Week_

requirements.heading: $WOYM$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$WOYM$` **Syntax:** `$WOYM$`

requirements.heading: $WOYM$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a number from 00-53, representing the week in the current year. Even though there are 52 weeks in a year, a week might not begin exactly on the first day of the year, so a maximum value for this variable can be 53 under these circumstances. For this variable, Monday is considered to be the first day of the week.

requirements.heading: $WOYM$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$WOYM$` **Returns:** `32`

requirements.heading: $YEAR$
requirements.text: _2 digit year_

requirements.heading: $YEAR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$YEAR$` **Syntax:** `$DOY$`

requirements.heading: $YEAR$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the two-digit number of the current year.

requirements.heading: $YEAR$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$YEAR$` **Returns:** `93`

requirements.heading: Sound related text variables (see 4.4)
requirements.text: The sound-generation family - [`$ALARM$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#alarm), [`$BEEP$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#beep), [`$BLIP$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#blip), [`$MUSIC$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#music), [`$PHASER$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#phaser), [`$REVPHASER$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#revphaser) and the chainable [`$T$`](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md#t) - is documented in [4.4 Tone & Sound Generation](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md).

requirements.heading: Sound related text variables (see 4.4)
requirements.text: All seven survive in 3.x: 2.00a4 defines optional parameters for every one of them (repeat counts, frequency/duration pairs, sweep parameters); the HLP confirms the DLL validates start/stop frequency ordering and rejects zero increments/durations, and SyncTERM implements the default (parameterless) behaviors, two of them with source comments reading `// Literally in the spec.` - full detail in [4.4](4.4-tone-and-sound-generation.md).

requirements.heading: Sound related text variables (see 4.4)
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP (tone-command error strings); SyncTERM (ripper.c:8235 `rv_sound`)._

requirements.heading: Mouse Related Text Variables
requirements.text: These text variables return information on, or manipulate the mouse in some fashion. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Mouse Related Text Variables
requirements.text: SyncTERM formats coordinate fields as **4 digits in graphics mode and 2 digits in text mode** - matching 2.00a4's rule that a text-window query returns text-cell coordinates in `XX`/`YY` form while graphics queries return `XXXX`/`YYYY`. _Evidence: SyncTERM (ripper.c:8290 `rv_mouse`; 8293, 8300 field widths); 2.00a4; HLP._

requirements.heading: $FIELDID$
requirements.text: _ID number of the current mouse field_

requirements.heading: $FIELDID$
requirements.text: _New in 3.x._

requirements.heading: $FIELDID$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$FIELDID$` **Syntax:** `$FIELDID$`

requirements.heading: $FIELDID$
requirements.text: Returns the ID number of the current mouse field - the counterpart of the `ID=n:` prefix on 3.x mouse-field [host commands](5.0-host-commands.md). Used by the demos for computed variable names (`$&MSG<<FIELDID>>$`).

requirements.heading: $FIELDID$
requirements.text: _Evidence: HLP; corpus (MENU.MSE)._

requirements.heading: $M$
requirements.text: _Mouse Button Status: LMR_

requirements.heading: $M$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$M$` **Syntax:** `$M$`

requirements.heading: $M$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a 3-character code representing the status of each mouse button. This variable works with two button and three button mice. The format of the code is LMR where L=Left, M=Middle (if any), and R=Right. If any button is clicked, the code for that button is "1". If the button is not depressed, it is "0". "100" would mean the left mouse button is depressed, but none of the others are.

requirements.heading: $M$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$M$` **Returns:** `001`

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: _Set the mouse cursor style number_

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MCURSOR(cursor_no)$`

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text:
```text
$MCURSOR(opt:CURSOR_NO)$
             ─────────
             0-6
             ─────────
         def=0
```

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: This command changes the current mouse cursor style to one of the pre-defined mouse cursor styles as defined in the [RIP_SET_MOUSE_CURSOR](4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#rip_set_mouse_cursor) command. The cursor_no parameter is identical to the cursor style numbers permitted for the RIPscrip command to alter the cursor. If you omit the CURSOR_NO parameter, the default "pointer" cursor is activated.

requirements.heading: $MCURSOR$
requirements.text: The demo scripts switch cursors on field entry/exit - `$MCURSOR(4)$` busy, `$MCURSOR(6)$` hand, `$MCURSOR(0)$` arrow. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP (`tvarProcMCURSOR`); corpus (DEMO-01.COL, MENU.FN)._

requirements.heading: $MSTAT$
requirements.text: _Mouse Status_

requirements.heading: $MSTAT$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MSTAT$` **Syntax:** `$MSTAT$`

requirements.heading: $MSTAT$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns a "YES" if there is a mouse installed on the RIPterm computer. If no mouse is installed, this variable returns "NO".

requirements.heading: $MSTAT$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MSTAT$` **Returns:** `YES`

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: _X Mouse location_

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$X(domain)$`

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text:
```text
$X(opt:DOMAIN)$
       ──────
       WORLD
       DEVICE
       ──────
   def=WORLD (except under "text mode query - see below)
```

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current X coordinate of the mouse pointer. This can be used interactively (for example, by on-line games) to determine the location of the mouse pointer. Only the X value of the mouse (X,Y) is returned. The value is 0000-9999 depending on what the current position is.

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: If this text variable is used inside a "text window query", then the X coordinate is returned in text cell coordinates based on the internal dimensions of the text window. This kind of result cannot happen unless the user clicks inside a text window's display area that has a text window query command in it, so there's no possibility for the coordinate to be out of bounds for that text window's dimensions. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: The results are in current world coordinates if no parameter is specified. If TYPE is "DEVICE" then the result is in raw video device coordinates. If TYPE is "WORLD" then the result is in desktop world coordinates. If the domain parameter is specified when this text variable is used in a text mode query, then it is explicitly overiding the "text coordinate" defaults of this command and returning the mouse coordinate information in the desired coordinate system. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $X$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$X(WORLD)$` - equivalent to `$X$` **Returns:** `0523`

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: _X/Y Mouse Location_

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$XY(domain)$`

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text:
```text
$XY(opt:DOMAIN)$
        ──────
        WORLD
        DEVICE
        ──────
    def=WORLD (except under text mode query - see below)
```

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns both the X and Y coordinates of the mouse pointer. A colon (:) separates the two values. The X and Y values may range from 0000-9999. The format that this value uses is: XXXX:YYYY

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: If this text variable is used inside a "text window query", then the X/Y coordinates are returned in text cell coordinates based on the internal dimensions of the text window. This kind of result cannot happen unless the user clicks inside a text window's display area that has a text window query command in it, so there's no possibility for the coordinate to be out of bounds for that text window's dimensions. The format that the coordinates are returned in is XX:YY where XX and YY can range from 00-99. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: The results are in current world coordinates if no parameter is specified. If TYPE is "DEVICE" then the results are in raw video device coordinates. If TYPE is "WORLD" then the results are in desktop world coordinates. If the domain parameter is specified when this text variable is used in a text mode query, then it is explicitly overiding the "text coordinate" defaults of this command and returning the mouse coordinate information in the desired coordinate system. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$XY(WORLD)$` - equivalent to `$XY$` **Returns:** `0297:0321`

requirements.heading: $XY$
requirements.text: > **Divergence:** 2.00a4 documents zero-padded _decimal_ output (`0297:0321`); SyncTERM emits **hexadecimal** (`%0*x:%0*x`). Which the shipping 3.0 driver used is unconfirmed _(hypothesis: decimal, per the documentation lineage)_. _(SyncTERM (ripper.c:8312-8320))_

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: _X, Y & button status_

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$XYM(domain)$`

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text:
```text
$XYM(opt:DOMAIN)$
         ──────
         WORLD
         DEVICE
         ──────
     def=WORLD (except under text mode query - see below)
```

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the X and Y coordinates of the mouse pointer, and which mouse buttons are pressed (if any). A colon (:) separates the three values. The X and Y values may range from 0000-9999. LMR stands for Left/Middle/Right. If any of these buttons are depressed (clicked), then the corresponding position will contain a 1. If a button is NOT depressed, then it will contain a 0. The format that this value uses is: XXXX:YYYY:LMR

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: If this text variable is used inside a "text window query", then the X/Y coordinates are returned in text cell coordinates based on the internal dimensions of the text window. This kind of result cannot happen unless the user clicks inside a text window's display area that has a text window query command in it, so there's no possibility for the coordinate to be out of bounds for that text window's dimensions. The format that the coordinates are returned in is XX:YY:LMR where XX and YY can range from 00-99. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: This means that the (X,Y) location of the cursor is (0123,0297), and that the Left and Middle buttons are depressed, but that the Right Mouse Button is not depressed.

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: The results are in current world coordinates if no parameter is specified. If TYPE is "DEVICE" then the results are in raw video device coordinates. If TYPE is "WORLD" then the results are in desktop world coordinates. If the domain parameter is specified when this text variable is used in a text mode query, then it is explicitly overiding the "text coordinate" defaults of this command and returning the mouse coordinate information in the desired coordinate system. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $XYM$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$XYM(WORLD)$` - Equivalent to `$XYM$` **Returns:** `0123:0297:110`

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: _Y Mouse location_

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$Y(domain)$`

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text:
```text
$Y(opt:DOMAIN)$
       ──────
       WORLD
       DEVICE
       ──────
   def=WORLD (except under text mode query - see below)
```

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the current Y coordinate of the mouse pointer. This can be used interactively (for example, by on-line games) to determine the location of the mouse pointer. Only the Y value of the Mouse (X,Y) is returned. The value is 0000-9999 depending on what the current position is.

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: If this text variable is used inside a "text window query", then the Y coordinate is returned in text cell coordinates based on the internal dimensions of the text window. This kind of result cannot happen unless the user clicks inside a text window's display area that has a text window query command in it, so there's no possibility for the coordinate to be out of bounds for that text window's dimensions. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: The results are in current world coordinates if no parameter is specified. If TYPE is "DEVICE" then the result is in raw video device coordinates. If TYPE is "WORLD" then the result is in desktop world coordinates. If the domain parameter is specified when this text variable is used in a text mode query, then it is explicitly overiding the "text coordinate" defaults of this command and returning the mouse coordinate information in the desired coordinate system. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $Y$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$Y(WORLD)$` - equivalent to `$Y$` **Returns:** `0244`

requirements.heading: Text Window Related Text Variables
requirements.text: These text variables return information on, or manipulate the text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Text Window Related Text Variables
requirements.text: The window-introspection group (`$TWX0$`/`$TWY0$`/`$TWX1$`/`$TWY1$`/`$TWW$`/`$TWH$`/`$TWIN$`/`$TWFONT$`) is confirmed for 3.x by SyncTERM's `rv_termstat` handler group; `$CURX$`/`$CURY$`/`$CURSOR$`/`$ISEXTWIN$` rest on the spec and help files, the management variables (`$ATW$`, `$MTW$`, `$TWGOTO$`, `$TWHOME$`, `$TWERASEEOL$`) are attested by the RIPTEL.HLP command-variable table, and the erase pair `$ETW$`/`$EGW$` by SyncTERM's `rv_erase`. The parameter grammar (window, type `BOUND`/`TEXT`/`CELL`, domain `WORLD`/`DEVICE`/`COLS`/`ROWS`) carries into 3.x unchanged as far as the evidence shows. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8734 `rv_termstat`; 8696 `rv_erase`)._

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: _Activates a text window definition_

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ATW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text:
```text
$ATW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: This command does the exact opposite of the [`$DTW$`](#dtw) text variable which deactivates a text window. When a window is activated, it no longer discards raw ANSI text that is sent to it. This does not make any visual changes on the screen immediately unless the current text window is the one activated, whereby the cursor might appear all of a sudden.

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to activate more than one text window in the same `$ATW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed.

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: If the text window being activated is protected, then it is not changed (ie, activated).

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: You may activate more then one window by specifying multiple text window slot numbers (0-35). You may also specify the following:

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                           |

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: | `ALL`   | Activate all text windows at once     |

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: | `CUR`   | Activate only the current text window |

requirements.heading: $ATW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ATW(CUR)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: _Disable the Text Cursor_

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$COFF(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text:
```text
$COFF(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
          ───────
          ALL
          CUR
          0-35
          ───────
      def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable turns off the text cursor in the specified text window(s). If that text window(s) is undefined or disabled, this this command does nothing for that parameter. If the window parameters are omitted, then the cursor in the current text window is displayed. If the window parameter(s) are specified, then they can be a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window, or the value of "ALL" to indicate that you wish to turn off the cursor in all text windows simultaneously. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: If you attempt to turn off a cursor in a text window that isn't defined, or that is deactivated, then that parameter does nothing. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: If any one of the parameters is invalid, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: If you turn off the cursor in a text window other than the current text window, then only the internal cursor status of that text window is altered. Since the cursor wouldn't be visible in that text window anyway, you wouldn't expect anything to visually happen on the screen. If you switch to that text window though, the cursor would not be displayed upon switching to it (normally it would). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$COFF$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $COFF$
requirements.text: `$COFF$$DTW$` is the standard demo-scene prologue. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8801 group); corpus (BLUEBACK.FN)._

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: _Enable the Text Cursor_

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$CON(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text:
```text
$CON(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable turns on the text cursor in the specified text window(s). If that text window is undefined or deactivated, this command does nothing. If the window parameter(s) are omitted, then the cursor in the current text window is displayed. If the window parameter is specified, then it can be a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window, or the value "ALL" to indicate all defined text windows (ie, in use). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: If you attempt to turn on a cursor in a text window that isn't defined, or that is deactivated, then that parameter does nothing. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: If any one of the parameters is invalid, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: If you turn on the cursor in a text window other than the current text window, then only the internal cursor status of that text window is altered - it will not be turned on until you switch to that text window. In this respect, only altering the current text window's cursor will actually make any immediate visible effect on the screen. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CON$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$CON$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: _Text Cursor Status_

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$CURSOR(window)$`

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text:
```text
$CURSOR(opt:WINDOW)$
            ──────
            CUR
            0-35
            ──────
        def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns "YES" if the Text Cursor is enabled in the specified text window, and "NO" if the Text Cursor is deactivated. If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is currently deactivated, then this command returns a value of "NO". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you specify the window number parameter, then you can specify a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or a value of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURSOR$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$CURSOR$` **Returns:** `YES`

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: _Text Cursor X Coordinate_

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$CURX(window)$`

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text:
```text
$CURX(opt:WINDOW)$
          ──────
          CUR
          0-35
          ──────
      def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the X coordinate of the text cursor in the specified text window, relative to the upper left of the Text Window. The location is "one based", so the first column of data is a value of "1", not "0". Typical return values for valid cursor locations could easily range from 1-91. If the specified text window is not defined, or is currently deactivated (via the [`$DTW$`](#dtw) command for example), then this text variable returns a value of "0" to indicate that the information isn't available. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you specify the window number parameter, then you can specify a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or a value of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURX$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$CURX(4)$` **Returns:** `2`

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: _Text Cursor Y Coordinate_

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$CURY(window)$`

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text:
```text
$CURY(opt:WINDOW)$
          ──────
          CUR
          0-35
          ──────
      def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns the Y coordinate of the text cursor in the specified text window, relative to the upper left of the Text Window. The location is "one based", so the first column of data is a value of "1", not "0". Typical return values for valid cursor locations could easily range from 1-43. If the specified text window is not defined, or is currently deactivated (via the [`$DTW$`](#dtw) command for example), then this text variable returns a value of "0" to indicate that the information isn't available. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you specify the window number parameter, then you can specify a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or a value of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $CURY$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$CURY(4)$` **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: _Deactivate Text Window_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$DTW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text:
```text
$DTW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified then the current text window is deactivated, preventing any received raw text from being displayed in that window. Switching to another text window data table entry can re-enable text displaying if that other window is "activated". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to disable more than one text window in the same `$DTW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If a slot (0-35) is specified then that text window slot is deactivated. This may or may not affect the current status of received text. If the slot specified just happens to be the current slot then all received text is deactivated. If the text window slot isn't the current text window then that text window is deactivated, but what is done with received raw text depends on the status of the current text window's status. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may specify "CUR" to explicitly deactivate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may also specify a slot of "ALL" to deactivate all defined text window slots. Text window data table entries that are not defined, or that are protected are not affected by this operation. This would also deactivate any raw text that is received because the act of deactivating all windows will consequently deactivate the current one too. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If the text window being deactivated is protected, then it is not changed (ie, deactivated). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: This command is useful in Host Commands when you click on a Mouse Field, it would halt any further output to the text window.

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DTW$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8726 `rv_disable`); corpus (14 uses)._

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: _Erase Text Window_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ETW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text:
```text
$ETW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: If no parameter(s) are specified then the current text window in use is cleared. If you specify a slot from 0-35 then the corresponding text window slot is erased. You may also specify "ALL" to erase all currently defined text window slots. Finally, you may specify the value of "CUR" to also indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the entire text window's bounding rectangle is erased, not just the display region inside the bounding rectangle. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to erase more than one text window in the same `$ETW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: If any text window specified aren't defined, or if the viewport is deactivated, then this command does nothing for that viewport parameter. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: This command is useful in Host Commands when you click on a Mouse Field, it could erase the text window THEN transmit the remainder of the Host Command (if any).

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ETW(ALL)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: _Is text window an extended text window?_

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A4._

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ISEXTWIN(windowno)$`

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text:
```text
$ISEXTWIN(opt:WINDOWNO)$
              ────────
              CUR
              0-35
              ────────
          def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: This text variable determines if the specified text window is an extended text window or not. If the WINDOWNO parameter is omitted, then it will inquire about the current text window. If WINDOWNO is specified, then it must be the value "CUR" for the current text window, or a window data table entry number from 0-35 to inquire about a specific text window data table entry.

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: If the specified text window is not defined, or deactivated, then this text variable returns a value of "-1". If it is an extended text window, then a "1" is returned, otherwise a "0" is returned to indicate that it is a standard (non-extended) text window.

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ISEXTWIN(5)$` **Returns:** `1`

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: _Maximize text window to full size_

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MTW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text:
```text
$MTW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: This command maximizes a particular text window to full screen using whatever text window font is associated with that text window. This does not affect any text that is already on the screen, only the internal definition of the text window (any scroll margins are reset). The cursor is moved to the home position, but is not re-enabled if it was previously disabled (use [`$CON$`](#con) for this). ANSI color attributes are not changed. The possible settings for the WHICH parameter are:

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | Keyword  | Description                                   |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `ALL`    | Maximize all text windows at once             |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `CUR`    | Maximize only the current text window         |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `number` | Maximize a particular text window slot number |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to maximize more than one text window in the same `$MTW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: It should be noted that if a text window being maximized is a standard text window created with the [RIP_TEXT_WINDOW](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_text_window) command, or if you just switched to a previously "unused" text window without explicitly defining it with a [RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_extended_text_window) command, then this command will treat the text window still as a "standard" text window. The window is moved to the very upper-left corner of the display. If it was an extended text window, then it is still moved to the upper-left corner of the screen, and the bounding box is made to exactly fit the actual text window display region. Remember, extended text windows don't know anything about text coordinate base locations of the upper-left corner, but standard text windows do. This command maintains this nature of the text window being maximized.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: If a text window being maximized is currently protected, this command also does nothing to that text window.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MTW(ALL)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: _Restore Text Window information_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RTW(source)$`

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text:
```text
$RTW(opt:SOURCE)$
         ──────
         BASE
         POP
         0-9
         ──────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified then this command restores all text window definitions from the slot-less definition file saved with a [`$STW$`](#stw) command (with no parameters). The file is not deleted and you can restore many times. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot parameter then that identifies which of the ten different slots you wish to restore from (0-9). Once the slot file is read it is deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "POP" then you are performing a stack-based pop operation (eg, `$RTW(POP)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number than the text window table will be restored from the text window backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: In any case, the text window settings active when a `$STW$` (Save Text Window) was executed are saved. The current cursor location, window location, ANSI attributes, cursor ON/OFF status, vertical scrolling margins, and the System Font are restored. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** The text contents of the window are not restored.

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RTW(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: _Save Text Window information_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$STW(destination)$`

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text:
```text
$STW(opt:DESTINATION)$
         ───────────
         BASE
         PUSH
         0-9
         ───────────
      def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified, then this command stores all currently defined text windows' settings base save area. The windows' X/Y dimensions are preserved, as are the current cursor location, ANSI attributes, cursor ON/OFF status and the vertical scrolling margins. Even the current System Fonts used for all windows are saved (if necessary). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot parameter, then you are specifying to save the text window definitions to one of up to ten different slots (0-9). These allow you to have up to ten different text window configurations saved at the same time. If you save to a slot then when you restore that slot the saved definitions are deleted from the disk. If you don't specify a slot parameter (a slot-less save) then you can restore that definition file multiple times without the file being deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "PUSH" then you are performing a stack-based save operation (eg, `$STW(PUSH)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number than the text window table will be stored into the text window backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** The contents of the Text Window are not saved.

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$STW(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: _Location of the last graphical text output_

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: _New in 3.x._

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TEXTXY$` **Syntax:** `$TEXTXY$`

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: Returns the location of the last graphical text output (X/Y). New in the 3.0 HLP inventory; return format unconfirmed _(hypothesis: `X:Y` pair like [`$XY$`](#xy))_.

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: _Evidence: HLP._

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: _Erase text window to line end_

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWERASEEOL(window1,window2`

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWERASEEOL(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
                ───────
                ALL
                CUR
                0-35
                ───────
            def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: This variable clears the current line in the specified text window from the cursor (inclusive) to the end of the line in the current ANSI color attributes. If the you specify no parameters, then the current text window is used for the destination window. If you do specify any parameters, they must be set to "CUR" for the current text window, "ALL" for all currently defined text windows, or 0-35 to indicate a specific text window slot number.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to erase more than one text window's current lines in the same `$TWERASEEOL$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: If the specified text window is deactivated or undefined then nothing happens for that parameter.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: Unlike many other text window commands, this one can make an actual visual effect on the screen even if the specified text window isn't the current text window.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWERASEEOL(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: _Active Text Font_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWFONT(window)$`

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWFONT(opt:WINDOW)$
            ──────
            CUR
            0-35
            ──────
        def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns which of the five Text Window Fonts is active, or 0 (zero) if specified text window is not defined, or is deactivated. The following values are returned: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | Value | Description          |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 0     | No Text Window       |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 2     | 91x43 MicroANSI font |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 4     | 91x25 MicroANSI font |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: Note that this command returns the actual text window font number plus one. So to match the returned value to actual RIPscrip text window font numbers, subtract one from this result (providing that it is greater than 0). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you do specify the window number parameter, then you may specify a value of 0-35 for a specific text window data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window (the default). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWFONT(4)$` **Returns:** `1`

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: The five values match the five terminal text modes listed in RIPtel's MESSAGES.HLP - fonts 2 and 4 are the 91-column [MicroANSI](../techspecs/3.3-microansi-maf-delta.md) modes. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8734 group)._

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: _Move cursor to X,Y in text window_

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWGOTO(winno,x_pos,y_pos)$`

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWGOTO(req:WINNO, opt:X_POS, opt:Y_POS)$
            ─────      ─────      ─────
            CUR        CUR        CUR
            0-35       0-90       0-42
                       ─────      ─────
                   def=CUR    def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: This variable allows you to move the cursor position in a given text window to a specified X/Y position. If no parameters are given or no X/Y parameters are given then nothing happens when this is executed.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then this command does nothing.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: The WINNO parameter specifies a text window data table entry to move the cursor in. Valid settings for WINNO are 0-35 for a specific text window data table entry, or "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified window is not the current text window then the cursor in that window's definition is moved but no visible things occur on the screen. If the specified window is "CUR" or the window number happens to be the current text window, then the cursor that is (potentially) on the screen is moved to the new location.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: The X/Y coordinates are text coordinates (1 based). Specifying both coordinates allows you to place the cursor anywhere in the chosen window. You may omit the Y parameter entirely to move the cursor horizontally only. Either the X or Y parameter (or both) may be specified as "CUR" to indicate the the row or column is not to change. In other words, if you wanted to move the cursor to line 2 in the text window 5, but leave its column unchanged, you would use `$TWGOTO(5,CUR,2)$`.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: If the goto sequence would put the cursor outside the dimensions of the text window then the cursor is placed at the closest point to the given location at the windows border.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: Text locations in this command are zero based (eg, the first column is specified as "0"). If the no X or Y parameters are specified, then this command does nothing because there is no X/Y information to move to.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWGOTO(CUR,10,2)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: _Text Window Height_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWH(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWH(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$
         ──────      ────      ──────
         CUR         BOUND     WORLD
         0-35        CELL      DEVICE
         ──────      TEXT      ROWS:TYPE=TEXT
     def=CUR         ────      ──────
                 def=TEXT  def=ROWS:TYPE=TEXT
                               WORLD:TYPE<>TEXT
```

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then this command returns the height of the current text window in text cells (lines). You may specify a window number to indicate which text window you are inquiring about. The text window number parameters may be a value from 0-35 to reference a specific text window data table entry, or you may specify a keyword of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then a value of "0" is returned. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you specify any parameters then they must be in a specific order. The first (already discussed) is the text window number, and if it is omitted, then the current text window is assumed. If you specify two parameters, then you must specify the window number parameter and the type parameter. The type parameter determines what type of information you are inquiring about. If you omit the type parameter then you are inquiring about the text window height itself, in actual text window cell sizes (eg, the window might respond with "5" to indicate that it is 5 lines of text tall. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you specify the type parameter, then you are directing this command to respond with information about a specific text window piece of information. The available type parameters are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                         |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `BOUND` | Return the height of the bounding box in pixels     |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Return the height of the display region             |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `CELL`  | Return the height of a text cell in the text window |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The third and final parameter is only of use if the BOUND or CELL parameter is used, and it determines the domain of the pixel size returned by the text variable. The possible values of domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `WORLD` | Return the value in world coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return the value in raw device pixel coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `ROWS` | Return height of area in text lines (valid only for a type of "TEXT". |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the height of the text window in lines of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The BOUND parameter refers to the text window's bounding rectangle. It is the absolute exterior that the text window may extend to. It can also be thought of as a margin outside the actual text window where nothing can be displayed from the text window. See the RIP*EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW for more details about this bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The CELL parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the height of a character cell used in the text window. The height of a cell is based on the font number and resolution currently in use on the actual destination RIPscrip software package. Under 640x350, this was typically 8x8 for font #0 (ie, in RIPscrip 1.54). This may be different now at varying resolutions. So, if you are running at a resolution of 640x350 and you inquire about a text window's cell height for a text window using font #0, then it most likely will return a result of 8 pixels (in device coordinates). The actual value in world coordinates could vary well be different based on the size of the world coordinate resolution frame. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The "TEXT" type indicates that you are requesting information about the text window sub-section of the text window definition. If the domain parameter is specified, then you are requesting the actual height of the text window display area in "lines of text". This can also be retrieved if the domain parameter is "ROWS". This particular domain parameter known as "ROWS" is only valid for a type parameter of "TEXT". Using it in any other context is considered a syntax error. If the domain parameter is specified, and it is set to "WORLD", then the pixel height of the display region is being requested in world coordinates. If domain is set to DEVICE, then you are requesting the height of the display region in actual hardware pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the bounding box of a text window can be obtained regardless of whether it is an old-style 1.54 text window created with RIP*TEXT_WINDOW or a new "resolution independent" text window defined via the RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW command. This can be because under the older text window concept, the bounding box is exactly as large as the text window itself, while under the extended text window, the text window will typically be inside the bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you completely omit the type parameter, then you must omit the domain parameter. In this case, you are asking for the height of the text window in "lines of text", not in pixels. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH$` - Height of current text window in lines of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(CUR)$` - Height of current text window in lines of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,BOUND)$` - Height of text window 5's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `800`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,BOUND,DEVICE)$` - Height of text window 5's bounding box in device pixel coordinates **Returns:** `400`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(CUR,CELL)` - Height of current text window's character cell in world coordinates. **Returns:** `16`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,CELL,DEVICE)$` - Height of text window 5's character cell in device pixel coordinates.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: _Move cursor to home position in text window_

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWHOME(winno)$`

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWHOME(opt:WINNO)$
            ─────
            CUR
            0-35
            ─────
        def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: This command moves the cursor in the specified text window data table entry to the upper-left corner of the window. WINNO may be any value from 0-35 to indicate the desired data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the WINNO slot number happens to correspond to the current text window or the WINNO parameter is specified as "CUR" then the cursor that is on the screen (potentially) will be visibly moved. If the WINNO parameter specifies a window that is not the current text window then the cursor position definition for that non-current window is altered only - no visible thing would happen on the screen.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: If the specified window is deactivated or is undefined then nothing happens.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: If the WINNO parameter is omitted then the current text window is assumed.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWHOME(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: _Text Window Status_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWIN(window)$`

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWIN(opt:WINDOW)$
          ──────
          CUR
          0-35
          ──────
      def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: This Text Variable checks to see if the specified Text Window is activated, and returns "YES" if the specified text window is activated or returns "NO" if it is deactivated (eg, with the [`$DTW$`](#dtw) command for example). If the specified text window isn't defined, then this command returns a value of "NO". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you do specify a window parameter then it can be a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWIN(4)$` **Returns:** `YES`

requirements.heading: $TWW$

requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWW(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWW(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$
         ──────      ────      ──────
         CUR         BOUND     WORLD
         0-35        CELL      DEVICE
         ──────      TEXT      COLS:TYPE=TEXT
     def=CUR         ────      ──────
                 def=TEXT  def=COLS:TYPE=TEXT
                               WORLD:TYPE<>TEXT
```

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then this command returns the width of the current text window in text cells (columns). You may specify a window number to indicate which text window you are inquiring about. The text window number parameters may be a value from 0-35 to reference a specific text window data table entry, or you may specify a keyword of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then a value of "0" is returned. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If you specify any parameters then they must be in a specific order. The first (already discussed) is the text window number, and if it is omitted, then the current text window is assumed. If you specify two parameters, then you must specify the window number parameter and the type parameter. The type parameter determines what type of information you are inquiring about. If you omit the type parameter then you are inquiring about the text window width itself, in actual text window cell sizes (eg, the window might respond with "5" to indicate that it is 5 columns wide. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If you specify the type parameter, then you are directing this command to respond with information about a specific text window piece of information. The available type parameters are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                        |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Return the width of the display region             |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `CELL`  | Return the width of a text cell in the text window |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: The third and final parameter is only of use if the BOUND or CELL parameter is used, and it determines the domain of the pixel size returned by the text variable. The possible values of domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `WORLD` | Return the value in world coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return the value in raw device pixel coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `COLS` | Return width of area in text columns (valid only for a type of "TEXT". |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the height of the text window in lines of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the width of the text window in columns of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

It can also be thought of as a margin outside the actual text window where nothing can be displayed from the text window. See the RIP*EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW for more details about this bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWW$

The width of a cell is based on the font number and resolution currently in use on the actual destination RIPscrip software package. Under 640x350, this was typically 8x8 for font #0 (ie, in RIPscrip 1.54). This may be different now at varying resolutions. So, if you are running at a resolution of 640x350 and you inquire about a text window's cell width for a text window using font #0, then it most likely will return a result of 8 pixels (in device coordinates). The actual value in world coordinates could vary well be different based on the size of the world coordinate resolution frame. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$

If the domain parameter is specified, then you are requesting the actual width of the text window display area in "columns of text". This can also be retrieved if the domain parameter is "COLS". This particular domain parameter known as "COLS" is only valid for a type parameter of "TEXT". Using it in any other context is considered a syntax error. If the domain parameter is specified, and it is set to "WORLD", then the pixel width of the display region is being requested in world coordinates. If domain is set to DEVICE, then you are requesting the width of the display region in actual hardware pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$

This can be because under the older text window concept, the bounding box is exactly as large as the text window itself, while under the extended text window, the text window will typically be inside the bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.text: If you completely omit the type parameter, then you must omit the domain parameter. In this case, you are asking for the width of the text window in "text columns", not in pixels. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW$` - Width of current text window in columns of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(CUR)$` - Width of current text window in columns of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(5,BOUND)$` - Width of text window 5's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `800`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(5,BOUND,DEVICE)$` - Width of text window 5's bounding box in device pixel coordinates **Returns:** `400`
